> **Note — transport retired.** The `OMP → Meridian (:3456)` path this page describes is RETIRED (renamed
> to `anthropic-direct`, EI-399 / 2026-06-12; OMP is unpublished), so the per-request token figures are
> historical for that path. The load-bearing lessons below — **keep the MCP tool surface lean + pin the
> `tools/list` manifest** (`tool-manifest.ts`), and the **EI-302 stale-schema boolean-coercion** gotcha —
> are transport-agnostic and current.

## What

Agents reach Anthropic as `OMP → Meridian (:3456) → @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk → api.anthropic.com`. Meridian holds the conversation as an SDK session and, **per turn, expands the request ~5×**: the client sends ~17k tokens, but the SDK inlines Claude Code's ~30k-char system prompt **plus every connected MCP tool schema** — measured at **288 tools ≈ 62k tokens, of which 246 are `papercusp-su`** (its full endpoint catalog, projected via `?superuser=1`). This ~62k base rides on **every** request, even a one-line follow-up.

The captured base (62,272 tok) matches the recurring `cache_read = 62,011` fingerprint in Meridian's `/telemetry/requests`.

## Why it matters

Cost is driven by cache **creation** (writes), not request size. In a real 24h sample, **~5 of 22 turns = ~75% of spend**, each reusing the ~62k base from cache but **re-creating 150–380k tokens** of accumulated history on top. A cache write costs ~12.5× a read, so concentrated busts dwarf everything else.

Busts are **reconnect-driven**: the SDK fetches `tools/list` once per connection, so when the operator hot-reloads while you're adding tools, the SDK reconnects, re-fetches a now-larger catalog, the inlined catalog bytes shift, and the whole prefix re-creates. (`papercusp-su` correctly does *not* emit `tools/list_changed`, so it's not notification-driven.)

Ruled out — a red herring: the `x-anthropic-billing-header` `cch=` hash in `system[0]` changes every request, but Anthropic excludes that block from the cache key, so it does **not** bust.

## How to apply

1. **Keep the MCP surface lean and stable.** Each tool schema is a permanent per-request tax; a flapping/reconnecting server re-creates the entire base. Don't hot-reload the operator during an expensive live session.
2. **Defer tools.** The Claude Agent SDK supports `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true` (only names inline, schemas fetched on demand) — measured **67.8k → 24.8k tok/request (−63%)**. Note: Meridian hardcodes this to `"false"` on the non-passthrough path, *suppressing* the SDK's own deferral.
3. **Pin the `tools/list` manifest** (commit `955ce391`): `packages/agent-mcp/src/tool-manifest.ts` freezes the exposed surface so a reconnect returns byte-identical bytes — adding tools during dev no longer busts a live session. Regenerate deliberately with `packages/agent-mcp/snapshot-tools.sh`, then restart the operator. Set `$AGENT_MCP_TOOL_MANIFEST` or `~/.papercusp/tool-manifest.json`; absent ⇒ expose all (no-op). Hand-edit the manifest down to curate the surface and shrink the base further.

## Gotcha: a pinned schema is a STALE schema — new args arrive as strings (EI-302)

The flip side of pinning the surface for cache stability: a long-lived session's tool **schema** is frozen too. So when you **add an arg to an existing tool**, every session that began before the change still sees the old schema and cannot type the new arg. The agent often still passes it (it read the source / docs / another agent's call), and because the value was never schema-typed it arrives as a **JSON string**.

For a boolean flag that means the wire value is `"true"`/`"false"`, and a bare `z.boolean()` rejects it — the dispatch layer (`libs/generic/tooldef/src/define-tool.ts`) throws **`invalid_args`**, with no obvious cause. The reporter's only workaround was hand-calling the raw HTTP MCP projection with a real boolean. This recurs for **any** new boolean flag, not just the one that surfaced it (EI-302 was `plans:new` `force`).

**Apply:** make a new boolean flag string-tolerant at the schema, but narrowly —

```ts
const stringTolerantBool = z.preprocess(
  (v) => (v === 'true' ? true : v === 'false' ? false : v),
  z.boolean(),
);
// force: stringTolerantBool.optional().describe(...)
```

Coerce **only** the two exact strings. Do **not** reach for `z.coerce.boolean()` — its `"false"` → `true` truthiness footgun is exactly why `_plans-args.ts` keeps an explicit boolean allowlist instead. A real boolean and a typo (`"yes"`, `1`) pass through to `z.boolean()` unchanged, so genuine mistakes still fail loudly. `z.toJSONSchema` renders the pipe's **output** side, so the advertised `tools/list` schema stays `type: boolean` (a stale session still failing on a wire string is the price of the pin, but a re-connected session sees a clean boolean). Reference fix + regression test: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/new.ts` + `…/plans/__tests__/new-force-coercion.test.ts`.

**Note — `force` now has dual responsibility (EI-134 / 2026-06-25).** The `plans:new` `force` arg has since grown a second job: when `force !== true`, creation is first rejected with `similar_exists` + the overlapping plans when existing slugs/titles share ≥2 topic tokens (audit P-049 / EI-134 — duplicate plans split project history). So `force: true` now bypasses both the dedup gate AND signals explicit intent when a stale session coerces the string `"true"`. The string-tolerant coercion applies transparently in both cases — a stale session passing `"true"` is coerced to `true` and correctly skips the dedup check.

**Role access update (2026-06-25):** `plans:new` changed from `agentRoles: [...SU_ROLES, 'cup']` to `agentRoles: [...AGENT_ROLES]` in the same batch — every built-in role can now call it. This does not affect the string-coercion or dedup behavior above, but means a wider set of sessions (worker, validator, etc.) may encounter the stale-schema `"true"` wire value when running against an old pinned manifest.
